questions.question: If 9 notebooks cost ₹135, how much will 20 notebooks of the same type cost?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Unitary Method** directly by calculating the price per unit.

Cost of 1 unit = 135 ÷ 9 = ₹15.

Cost of 20 units = 20 × 15 = ₹300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 9 **notebooks** = ₹135

Required quantity = 20 **notebooks**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a9cd1b7cdb0eb361c5406353730a6f6b917b302b73fbac23a5bb196346985964.png] 

**Formula Used:**

In **Direct Proportion**: (Price₁ ÷ Quantity₁) = (Price₂ ÷ Quantity₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 135 ÷ 9 = Price₂ ÷ 20

⇒ 15 = Price₂ ÷ 20

⇒ Price₂ = 15 × 20

⇒ Price₂ = ₹300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

Two quantities are in **direct proportion** if an increase in one leads to a corresponding increase in the other such that their ratio remains constant (x/y = k).

Unitary Method

The **unitary method** involves finding the value of a single unit first and then multiplying that value by the required number of units to find the total.

Ratio Application

The ratio of quantities (9 : 20) must be equal to the ratio of their costs (135 : x), which helps solve **partnership** and **mixture** problems as well.

questions.question:
Find the value of m which satisfies

 ((23)/(5))¹³ times ((5)/(23))⁹ times ((23)/(5))⁵ = ((5)/(23))⁶m ⁺ ⁹
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all terms to a common **base** of (5/23) using the **reciprocal rule**: (a/b)ⁿ = (b/a)−ⁿ.

LHS net exponent = −13 + 9 − 5 = −9.

Equate the exponents of both sides: 6m + 9 = −9.

6m = −18 ⇒ m = −3.

**∴ The correct answer is -3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** (23/5)¹³ × (5/23)⁹ × (23/5)⁵ = (5/23)⁶m ⁺ ⁹

**Laws of Exponents Used:** 1. am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ | 2. (a/b)ⁿ = (b/a)−ⁿ

⇒ ((5/23)−¹)¹³ × (5/23)⁹ × ((5/23)−¹)⁵ = (5/23)⁶m ⁺ ⁹

⇒ (5/23)−¹³ × (5/23)⁹ × (5/23)−⁵ = (5/23)⁶m ⁺ ⁹

⇒ (5/23)−¹³ ⁺ ⁹ − ⁵ = (5/23)⁶m ⁺ ⁹

⇒ (5/23)−⁹ = (5/23)⁶m ⁺ ⁹

Since the **bases are equal**, we equate the **exponents**:

⇒ −9 = 6m + 9

⇒ 6m = −9 − 9

⇒ 6m = −18

⇒ m = −18/6

⇒ m = −3

**∴ The correct answer is -3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Law of Exponents

When multiplying expressions with the same base, simply add the exponents: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ.

Negative Exponent Rule

A fraction raised to a negative power is equal to its reciprocal raised to the corresponding positive power: (a/b)−ⁿ = (b/a)ⁿ.

Power Equality Property

If ax = ay and a is not equal to 0, 1, or −1, then the exponents must be equal, i.e., x = y.

questions.question:
A sum of money amounts to ₹19,360 in 3 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually. The compound interest (in ₹) earned is

(Round off your answer to the nearest paise.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **effective interest rate** for 10% compounded annually for **3 years** is 33.1%.

Total **Amount percentage** = 100% + 33.1% = 133.1%.

Given, 133.1% = ₹19,360.

**Compound Interest** (33.1%) = (19,360 ÷ 133.1) × 33.1 = ₹4814.5454...

Rounding to the **nearest paise**, we get ₹4814.55.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4814.55.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amount (A)** = ₹19,360

**Rate (r)** = 10% per annum

**Time (n)** = 3 years

**Formula Used:** A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ and CI = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/44c912e512a5a6f6003e958213418f95f9388de6d39375753da88f04c6c5f117.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 19,360 = P(1 + 10/100)³

⇒ 19,360 = P(11/10)³

⇒ 19,360 = P × (1331/1000)

⇒ P = (19,360 × 1000) ÷ 1331

⇒ P = 14545.4545...

⇒ CI = Amount − Principal

⇒ CI = 19,360 − 14545.4545...

⇒ CI = 4814.5454...

⇒ CI ≈ ₹4814.55 (rounded to nearest paise)

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4814.55.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The formula for Compound Interest is CI = P[(1 + R/100)ⁿ − 1], where P is principal, R is rate, and n is time.

Effective Rate for 10%

For 2 years, the effective rate is 21%. For 3 years, the effective rate is 33.1%.

SI vs CI Difference (2 Years)

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is given by D = P(R/100)².

Rounding Rules

Rounding to the nearest paise means keeping two decimal places. If the third decimal is 5 or more, increase the second decimal by 1.

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 180 km in 3 hours. Find its average speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Average Speed** of an object is simply the **Total Distance** divided by the **Total Time** taken.

**Average Speed** = 180 ÷ 3 = 60 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **Distance** covered by the car = 180 km

Total **Time** taken = 3 hr

**Formula Used:**

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c8be99aded855e7715c5745b0ad0b90abe4160053d7ba2ba74f605c2d3059f0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average Speed = 180 ÷ 3

⇒ Average Speed = 60 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Distance Formula

Speed is defined as the rate of change of distance with respect to time. Formula: Speed = Distance ÷ Time.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If a body travels two equal distances at speeds **u** and **v**, then the average speed for the whole journey is 2uv ÷ (u + v).

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a body travels for two equal time intervals at speeds **u** and **v**, the average speed is (u + v) ÷ 2.

questions.question: The sum of two positive numbers is 77 and their product is 1392. The positive difference between them is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the numbers be x and y. Given **Sum (x + y) = 77** and **Product (xy) = 1392**.

Use the direct relation: **Difference = √((Sum)² − 4 × Product)**.

Difference = √(77² − 4 × 1392) = √(5929 − 5568).

Difference = √361 = **19**.

**∴ The correct answer is 19.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two positive numbers (x + y) = **77**

Product of the numbers (xy) = **1392**

**Formula Used:**

The relationship between sum, product, and difference is: **(x − y)² = (x + y)² − 4xy**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f08f1033cd80e59007f64a29ea423c8f9ce754074ac255238be0c45f6d9eaa4e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x − y)² = (77)² − 4 × 1392

⇒ (x − y)² = 5929 − 5568

⇒ (x − y)² = 361

⇒ x − y = √361

⇒ x − y = 19

**∴ The correct answer is 19.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Useful variations include (x + y)² + (x − y)² = 2(x² + y²) and (x + y)² − (x − y)² = 4xy.

Quadratic Equation Relation

The numbers x and y are the roots of the quadratic equation t² − (Sum)t + (Product) = 0. Here, t² − 77t + 1392 = 0.

Perfect Squares

Memorizing squares up to 30 is vital for competitive exams; for instance, 18² = 324, 19² = 361, and 20² = 400.

questions.question: Riya and Neha have certain amount of money. If Riya gives ₹20 to Neha, then Riya will have three times as much money as Neha. However, if Neha gives ₹40 to Riya, then Riya will have five times as much money as Neha. What is the total amount of money (in ₹) that Riya and Neha initially had together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **total amount** of money be T.

Since money is only transferred internally, the **total sum** T remains constant.

Case 1: Ratio R:N is 3:1 ⇒ **Neha** has T ÷ 4 of the total money.

Case 2: Ratio R:N is 5:1 ⇒ **Neha** has T ÷ 6 of the total money.

The difference in **Neha**'s money between the two cases is 20 − (−40) = 60.

⇒ T/4 − T/6 = 60 ⇒ T/12 = 60 ⇒ T = 60 × 12 = 720.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹720.**

questions.question: In a parallelogram, the difference of two adjacent angles is 40°. Find the measure of the smaller angle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **parallelogram**, the sum of any two **adjacent angles** is always 180°.

Given the **difference** between these two angles is 40°.

Smaller angle = (Sum of angles − Difference of angles) ÷ 2

Smaller angle = (180° − 40°) ÷ 2 = 140° ÷ 2 = 70°.

**∴ The correct answer is 70degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Difference between **adjacent angles** = 40°.

**Formula Used:** Adjacent angles of a **parallelogram** are **supplementary** (sum = 180°).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70f557577146e589097614b471e65ac7631a5a88435174a492903b4d540f69b9.png] 

Let the larger angle be **x** and the **smaller angle** be **y**.

⇒ x + y = 180° ... (i)

⇒ x − y = 40° ... (ii)

Subtracting equation (ii) from (i):

⇒ (x + y) − (x − y) = 180° − 40°

⇒ 2y = 140°

⇒ y = 140° ÷ 2

⇒ y = 70°

**∴ The correct answer is 70degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Adjacent Angles Property

In any **parallelogram**, consecutive or **adjacent angles** are supplementary, meaning their sum is always 180°.

Opposite Angles Property

In a **parallelogram**, the **opposite angles** are always equal in measure (e.g., ∠A = ∠C and ∠B = ∠D).

Sum of Interior Angles

For any **quadrilateral**, the sum of all four **interior angles** is exactly 360°.

questions.question: The cost of a certain fabric is directly proportional to its length for a given width. If the cost of 8 meters of the fabric is ₹3,200, what will be the cost of 25 meters of the same fabric?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **cost** is **directly proportional** to **length**:

Ratio of lengths = 8 : 25

Ratio of costs = 8 : 25

8 units = ₹3,200 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹400

25 units = 25 × 400 = ₹10,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial length (L₁) = 8 m

Initial cost (C₁) = ₹3,200

Target length (L₂) = 25 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ea7648c63f06ee816d612fc4a1734b6ceca9891378f21396fe622ec9af0b0c6.png] 

**Formula Used:**

For **direct proportion**: C₁ ÷ L₁ = C₂ ÷ L₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3,200 ÷ 8 = C₂ ÷ 25

⇒ 400 = C₂ ÷ 25

⇒ C₂ = 400 × 25

⇒ C₂ = 10,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

Two quantities x and y are in direct proportion if the ratio x/y remains constant. Formula: x₁/y₁ = x₂/y₂.

Inverse Proportion

Two quantities are in inverse proportion if their product remains constant. Formula: x₁ × y₁ = x₂ × y₂.

Unitary Method

A technique where you find the value of a **single unit** (by division) and then find the necessary value by multiplication.

questions.question:
Find the median of the following data (correct to two places of decimal).

 
 

 Class interval
 0-6
 6-12
 12-18
 18-24
 24-30
 30-36
 
 

 Frequency
 5
 7

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total frequency **N = 52**, so **N/2 = 26**.

Cumulative frequency (CF) for class 12-18 is 22, and for 18-24 is 35.

The **median class** is **18−24** where L = 18, CF = 22, f = 13, and h = 6.

Median = 18 + ((26 − 22) ÷ 13) × 6 = 18 + (4 × 6) ÷ 13 = 18 + 1.846...

**∴ The correct answer is 19.85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Data:**

 
 

 **Class Interval**
 **Frequency (f)**
 **Cumulative Frequency (CF)**
 
 

 0−6
 5
 5
 
 

 6−12
 7
 12
 
 

 12−18
 10
 22
 
 

 **18−24**
 **13**
 **35**
 
 

 24−30
 9
 44
 
 

 30−36
 8
 52
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b39d6e04b875faccb43a7f448a7f099b35f27ce4609ad8716351387df12ebfa9.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Median = L + [((N ÷ 2) − CF) ÷ f] × h

Where:

L = Lower limit of median class = 18

N = Total frequency = 52

CF = Cumulative frequency of the class preceding the median class = 22

f = Frequency of the median class = 13

h = Class width = 6

**Calculations:**

⇒ N ÷ 2 = 52 ÷ 2 = 26

⇒ Median = 18 + [(26 − 22) ÷ 13] × 6

⇒ Median = 18 + [4 ÷ 13] × 6

⇒ Median = 18 + (24 ÷ 13)

⇒ Median = 18 + 1.84615...

⇒ Median ≈ 19.846

**∴ The correct answer is 19.85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

Relationship between mean, median, and mode: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Median Class Identification

The median class is the class interval whose cumulative frequency is just greater than or equal to **N/2**.

Mean of Grouped Data

The mean (μ) is calculated using Σfᵢxᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ is the class mark.

Mode for Grouped Data

Mode = L + [(f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h.

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offers the following schemes on toys of the same marked price.

(A) Successive discounts of 18% and 39% on any number of toys bought.

(B) Successive discounts of 29%, 45% and 4% on any number of toys bought.

(C) 29% discount on the first 8 toys and 31% discount on each toy thereon.

(D) 7 toys free of cost on buying 8 toys.

A customer wants to buy 8 toys. Which of the above schemes is the least beneficial to her?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare the **net discount percentage** for each scheme to find the **least beneficial** (lowest discount):

Scheme A: 18 + 39 − (18 × 39)/100 = 57 − 7.02 = **49.98%**

Scheme B: Net multiplier = 0.71 × 0.55 × 0.96 ≈ 0.375 ⇒ Discount ≈ **62.5%**

Scheme C: For 8 toys, the discount is a flat **29%**.

Scheme D: 7 free on 8 bought ⇒ 7/15 × 100 ≈ **46.67%**

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number of toys to buy = 8. All toys have the same **Marked Price (MP)**.

**Formula Used:**

1. Successive discounts x% and y% = [x + y − (xy/100)]%

2. Buy X, Get Y Free discount % = [Y / (X + Y)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c37753bf1edf5edaa9e7f1270d14ecc401d184f3a8345f548710588b80125e81.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ **Scheme A:** Net Discount = 18 + 39 − (18 × 39 / 100) = 57 − 7.02 = 49.98%

⇒ **Scheme B:** Successive 29%, 45%, 4%. Price multiplier = 0.71 × 0.55 × 0.96 = 0.37488. Discount = (1 − 0.37488) × 100 = 62.512%

⇒ **Scheme C:** Customer buys exactly 8 toys. Discount offered on the first 8 toys = 29%.

⇒ **Scheme D:** Buy 8, Get 7 Free. Total toys = 15. Discount = (7 / 15) × 100 = 46.67%

⇒ Comparing all: 29% (C) [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

The effective discount for two successive discounts a% and b% is calculated as [a + b − (ab/100)]%. For three or more, use the multiplier method: 100 − [100 × (100−d₁)/100 × (100−d₂)/100 × ...].

Buy X Get Y Free

In this retail scheme, the customer pays for X items but receives X + Y items in total. The discount percentage is (Free Items / Total Items) × 100 = [Y / (X + Y)] × 100.

Customer vs. Shopkeeper Benefit

A customer always seeks the **maximum discount** (most beneficial), while the shopkeeper seeks the **minimum discount** to maximize profit.

questions.question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 4 hours and 18 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 18 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-fourth of the empty cistern if all the taps are opened together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Tap 2** fills (18 hr) and **Tap 3** empties (18 hr) at the same rate.

Their net contribution to the **cistern** is zero (1/18 − 1/18 = 0).

Only **Tap 1** effectively fills the **cistern** at a rate of 4 hr per full tank.

Time required to fill **one-fourth** of the **cistern** = 4 hr × 1/4 = 1 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] Alternate Method&l

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 5 : 14 : 9, and their LCM is 7560. Their HCF is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**LCM** of ratio parts 5, 14, and 9 = 5 × 14 × 9 = 630 units.

Given **LCM** = 7560.

1 ratio unit (which represents the **HCF**) = 7560 ÷ 630 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of three numbers = 5 : 14 : 9

**LCM** of the numbers = 7560

**Formula Used:**

For numbers in ratio a : b : c, the **LCM** of the numbers is given by: x × **LCM**(a, b, c), where **x** is the **HCF**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/57b238795677c488645dc4ee1c472e22ee1f3762d01d2cd5190df4481b28e91d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the numbers be 5x, 14x, and 9x, where **x** is the **HCF**.

⇒ **LCM**(5x, 14x, 9x) = x × **LCM**(5, 14, 9)

⇒ Since 5, 14, and 9 are **pairwise co-prime**, their **LCM** = 5 × 14 × 9 = 630.

⇒ Given **LCM** = 7560

⇒ 630 × x = 7560

⇒ x = 7560 ÷ 630

⇒ x = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers **a** and **b**, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM** (a × b = **HCF** × **LCM**).

Co-prime Numbers

Numbers are said to be **co-prime** if their **HCF** is 1. If ratio parts are co-prime, their **LCM** is simply their product.

LCM and HCF of Fractions

**LCM** of fractions = **LCM** of numerators ÷ **HCF** of denominators; **HCF** of fractions = **HCF** of numerators ÷ **LCM** of denominators.

questions.question: Sarang invested a certain sum of money at 10% per annum. After 2 years, he received ₹178.5 as compound interest, compounded annually. Find the corresponding simple interest (in ₹) for 2 years at the same rate.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net **Compound Interest (CI)** rate for **2 years** at **10%** = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%.

Net **Simple Interest (SI)** rate for **2 years** at **10%** = 10 × 2 = 20%.

Ratio of CI to SI = 21 : 20.

Given 21 units = ₹178.5 ⇒ 1 unit = 178.5 ÷ 21 = 8.5.

Value of 20 units (SI) = 20 × 8.5 = ₹170.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹170.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Rate (R) = 10%, Time (T) = 2 years, Compound Interest (CI) = ₹178.5.

**Formula Used:** CI = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1] and SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e7316173a35c3a61350c837dc298abf9cf8385384ddc6be8701f2d7c63b194e9.png] 

⇒ CI = P[(1 + 10/100)² − 1]

⇒ 178.5 = P[(1.1)² − 1]

⇒ 178.5 = P[1.21 − 1]

⇒ 178.5 = 0.21P

⇒ P = 178.5 ÷ 0.21 = ₹850

⇒ SI = (850 × 10 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 850 × 0.2 = ₹170

**∴ The correct answer is ₹170.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference (D) is given by the formula D = P × (R/100)².

CI and SI Ratio for 2 years

The ratio of Compound Interest to Simple Interest for 2 years is CI / SI = (200 + R) / 200.

Effective Rate of Interest

For CI, the effective rate for two successive years x% and y% is [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

questions.question: The price of an article increases and decreases alternately by 20% every year. If the difference between the prices at the end of the second year and third year is ₹1,920, find 40% of the price (in ₹) of the article at the end of the first year.
questions.solution:
Let the initial price be P.

Price at end of 1st year (P1) = P × 1.20

Price at end of 2nd year (P2) = P1 × 0.80 = 0.96 P1

Price at end of 3rd year (P3) = P2 × 1.20 = 1.152 P1

Difference |P3 - P2| = |1.152 P1 - 0.96 P1| = 0.192 P1

0.192 P1 = 1920

P1 = 10,000

40% of P1 = 0.40 × 10,000 = ₹4,800.

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 7 decorative lamps for ₹2,850. Due to damage, 2 lamps could not be sold. He sold the remaining lamps at ₹360 each. What is his total loss (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
Cost Price (CP) = ₹2,850

Number of lamps sold = 7 - 2 = 5

Selling Price (SP) = 5 × 360 = ₹1,800

Loss = CP - SP = 2,850 - 1,800 = ₹1,050.

If p is a prime number and GCD (p²−1, p²+1) = 2, then the value of p must be:
questions.solution:
If p = 2, p²-1 = 3 and p²+1 = 5. GCD(3, 5) = 1.

If p is any odd prime, p² is odd, so p²-1 and p²+1 are consecutive even numbers. The GCD of any two consecutive even numbers is always 2.

questions.question: Three automatic doors in a metro station undergo system checks at regular intervals of 14 minutes, 18 minutes, and 21 minutes, respectively. If all three doors are checked together at the start, after how many minutes will they be checked together again for the first time?
questions.solution:
The time they will be checked together again is the LCM of 14, 18, and 21.

14 = 2 × 7

18 = 2 × 3²

21 = 3 × 7

LCM = 2 × 3² × 7 = 2 × 9 × 7 = 126 minutes.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells a watch for ₹840 after giving a 30% discount. What was the marked price (in ₹) of the watch?
questions.solution:
Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 - Discount)%

840 = MP × 70/100

MP = (840 × 100) / 70 = 12 × 100 = ₹1,200.

40 persons begin to work together on a job. But after some days 10 persons left the work. As a result, the job which should have been completed in 50 days is completed in 60 days. How many days after the commencement of the work did the 10 persons leave?
questions.solution:
Total work = 40 × 50 = 2000 man-days.

Let the 10 persons leave after 'd' days.

Work done in 'd' days = 40d.

Remaining work done by 30 persons in (60 - d) days = 30(60 - d).

40d + 1800 - 30d = 2000

10d = 200

d = 20 days.

Five years ago, the age of Kavita was one-third of the present age of her mother. After 5 years, the sum of their ages will be 75 years. What is Kavita’s present age?
questions.solution:
Let Kavita's present age be K and Mother's be M.

K - 5 = M/3 => M = 3K - 15.

(K + 5) + (M + 5) = 75 => K + M = 65.

K + (3K - 15) = 65

4K = 80

K = 20 years.
